original_question: Given a function kappa in C^-1(0,+infinity), what conditions are necessary and sufficient for kappa to belong to the class L1 of Sonine-kernel pairs, and how can one derive an explicit representation of the associated kernel k that satisfies the Sonine relation (kappa * k)(t) = 1 for t > 0?
target_in_paper: Section 2.4, open problem 6, with notation fixed by Section 2.3, Eq. (31) and Definition 1 (Eqs. (36)–(37)).
correct_elements: The draft already captures the correct local target in the paper: it asks about a kernel κ on (0,+∞) lying in C_{-1}(0,+∞), seeks conditions for κ to belong to the Sonine-kernel class L1, and asks for a representation of the associated kernel k satisfying the Sonine relation (κ*k)(t)=1 for t>0. This is very close to the wording of Section 2.4, open problem 6.
missing_details: The paper’s official formulation is an open problem in Section 2.4, item 6, not a theorem or proposition.
The draft does not state the exact meaning of L1 from Definition 1: (κ, k ∈ L1) iff (κ, k ∈ C_{-1,0}(0,+∞)) and ((κ*k)(t) = {1}) for t > 0.
The draft uses κ ∈ C_{-1}(0,+∞), but Definition 1 requires the sharper regularity κ, k ∈ C_{-1,0}(0,+∞) once κ is actually in L1; this distinction should be made explicit.
The paper defines C_{α,β}(0,+∞) by C_{α,β}(0,+∞) = {f : f(t) = t^p f1(t), t > 0, α < p < β, f1 ∈ C[0,+∞)}; in particular, C_{-1}(0,+∞) means C_{-1,+∞}(0,+∞).
The convolution must be specified as the Laplace convolution on the positive semi-axis: (f*g)(t) = ∫_0^t f(t-τ)g(τ) dτ.
The paper writes the right-hand side as {1}, i.e. the constant function equal to 1 on t > 0; the draft suppresses this notation.
The draft asks for an explicit representation, but the paper only says derive a representation; asking for more than that slightly overstates the official formulation.

To be fully stand-alone, the question should make clear that the unknown is the existence and description of some associated kernel k in C_{-1,0}(0,+∞), not merely any function solving the convolution equation outside that class.

The nearby context is that kernels from L1 underlie the GFI/GFD framework and the 1st and 2nd Fundamental Theorems of fractional calculus; this explains why this characterization problem is being asked.
refined_question: Let C_{α,β}(0,+∞) := {f : f(t) = t^p f1(t) for t > 0, with α < p < β and f1 ∈ C[0,+∞)}, let C_{-1}(0,+∞) := C_{-1,+∞}(0,+∞), and let (f*g)(t) := ∫_0^t f(t-τ)g(τ) dτ denote the Laplace convolution on (0,+∞). Characterize those kernels κ ∈ C_{-1}(0,+∞) for which there exists an associated kernel k ∈ C_{-1,0}(0,+∞) such that (κ*k)(t) = {1} for all t > 0; equivalently, determine when the pair (κ,k) belongs to the class L1 defined by (κ, k ∈ L1) iff (κ, k ∈ C_{-1,0}(0,+∞)) and ((κ*k)(t) = {1}), and derive a representation for the associated kernel k.
equivalent_formulation: Characterize all κ ∈ C_{-1}(0,+∞) for which there exists k ∈ C_{-1,0}(0,+∞) satisfying the Sonine relation ∫_0^t κ(t-τ)k(τ) dτ = 1 for every t > 0, and derive a representation of that associated kernel k.
justification: The nearest official target is Section 2.4, item 6, whose wording is essentially the same as the draft. To make the question fully self-contained and faithful to the paper, one must import the exact Sonine relation from Eq. (31), the function-space notation C_{α,β}(0,+∞) and the pair-based definition of L1 from Definition 1, and the surrounding GFI/GFD context from Theorems 5 and 6. The refined question stays narrow: it does not broaden from L1 to Ln, does not add hypotheses absent from the paper, and only sharpens the notation and scope that the paper leaves implicit in the open-problem statement.
